ai_technology: MatEvolve; Claude Fable 5 agent with motif editing and first-principles validation

evidence.ai_role: A frozen learned language model translates crystals into motif profiles and edits profiles to propose structures; an evidence-based recommender prioritizes candidates for DFT.
evidence.tested: Within-study DFT structural relaxation/stability and magnetic-property calculations; original v1 selected 300 of 600 proposals and found 63 joint-target candidates. Later ResearchSquare run selected 400 of 800 and found 80.
evidence.unknown: No experimental synthesis or measured magnetic performance established. Validation budgets do not equalize proposal pools/ranking methods; database-relative novelty is not proof of absolute originality.

organization: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Institute of Science Tokyo; The Institute of Statistical Mathematics; Tohoku University

source_review.scope: Original arXiv v1 primary HTML: date, agent operation, design settings, Table1/S2, first-principles evaluation and novelty rules; later ResearchSquare full manuscript Methods/results independently read. Actual version differences explicitly retained; no figures imported from later run into v1.

summary: MatEvolve uses Claude Fable 5 to edit crystal motif descriptions and generate rare-earth-lean magnet candidates, with first-principles calculations assessing selected designs. The August 16 first preprint reported 63 of 300 selected candidates meeting its joint stability, uniqueness, database-novelty, magnetization and new-prototype criteria. The November 23 ResearchSquare version expands the run to 400 selected candidates and reports 80 meeting its joint target; these versions are the same study, not independent replication. Results are DFT-computed candidates, not experimentally synthesized or measured magnets; novelty is relative to the specified databases and structural-matching rules.
title: MatEvolve designs candidate magnetic crystals with new structural prototypes
